summary: Genuinely mutual NDA that largely tracks the playbook, with possible deviations only on the carve-out evidence standard, the independent-development carve-out, insurers in Representatives, compelled-disclosure cost allocation, and an unmapped breach-notification duty.

findings.quote: each Party, acting as the Receiving Party, hereby covenants, undertakes and agrees with the other Party, acting as the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Obligations bind each Party as Receiving Party and protect each as Disclosing Party, and the definitions in 1.1.4, 1.1.6 and 1.1.9 let either party take either role.

findings.quote: whether disclosed before, on or after the Effective Date, in connection with the Purpose
findings.why: Covers information of either party disclosed in connection with the Purpose and, at 1.1.4(d), derived notes and analyses, though it has no marked-or-reasonably-confidential limiter.

findings.quote: use the Confidential Information exclusively for the furtherance of the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, a potential commercial transaction and collaboration between the parties.

findings.quote: can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous written records, documentary evidence or other competent proof
findings.why: The Receiving Party must conclusively prove an exception with contemporaneous records, which is stricter than the 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard the playbook accepts and so narrows all four carve-outs.
findings.draft_redline: which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer the usual 'written records or reasonable evidence' standard for the exclusions, as a requirement of conclusive, contemporaneous proof would be difficult for either party to meet.

findings.quote: was independently developed by employees, agents or contractors of the Receiving Party who had no access to
findings.why: Independent development is available only if the developers had no access to the Confidential Information, which narrows the standard carve-out.
findings.draft_redline: was independently developed by or for the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to word the independent-development exclusion by reference to non-use of the Confidential Information, rather than to developers having had no access, so that it works equally for both parties.

findings.quote: the directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party
findings.why: Representatives (and, via Affiliates, Group members) cover advisers and auditors on a need-to-know basis, but insurers are not listed, so the playbook's insurer limb is not met.
findings.draft_redline: the directors, officers, employees, professional advisers, auditors, insurers, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party
findings.note_to_counterparty: Could we add insurers to the list of permitted Representatives? Each party may need to share information with its insurers on a confidential basis.

findings.quote: are bound by written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of secrecy
findings.why: Recipients need written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of secrecy, which fits the accepted undertaking requirement.
findings.fallback_cited: Requirement for written confidentiality undertakings from advisers who are not under professional duties.

findings.quote: remain fully and unconditionally liable to the Disclosing Party for any breach of the terms of this Agreement caused by any act, omission, default or negligence of any of its Representatives
findings.why: The Receiving Party is liable for its Representatives and Affiliates, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall, subject to applicable legal restrictions:
findings.why: Disclosure compelled by law, court, regulator or stock exchange is covered, with notice and cooperation qualified by applicable legal restrictions and 4.2 handling cases where notice is prohibited.

findings.quote: exercise all reasonable commercial efforts to obtain a binding written assurance from the presiding court, tribunal or regulatory agency that confidential treatment will be accorded
findings.why: The Receiving Party must seek confidential treatment and cooperate under 4.1.2 without any statement that this is at the Disclosing Party's cost, whereas the playbook accepts reasonable endeavours only at the Disclosing Party's cost.
findings.draft_redline: exercise reasonable endeavours, at the Disclosing Party's cost, to obtain confidential treatment of the disclosed Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to make clear that cooperation and any steps to resist or limit a compelled disclosure are at the cost of the party whose information is concerned.

findings.quote: within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such request
findings.why: Return or destruction within 10 Business Days of written request, with officer certification at 5.2 and a backup and archival-copy exception at 5.3 with continued confidentiality at 5.4.

findings.quote: electronic backup copies of Confidential Information generated automatically through routine data archiving, disaster recovery and electronic backup systems
findings.why: Automated backups may be retained and remain confidential under 5.4, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting, conferring, assigning or transferring
findings.why: No IP, licence or ownership passes to the Receiving Party, and there is no feedback, improvements or derivatives clause.

findings.quote: without any representation, warranty or guarantee of any kind
findings.why: Mutual 'as is' and no-warranty disclaimers at 6.2 and 6.3, with no fraud exclusion being removed.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: shall constitute, create, imply or evidence an obligation by either Party to enter into any further commercial agreement
findings.why: Mutual statement that there is no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: is not intended to involve the transfer, sharing or processing of any personal data
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details.

findings.quote: execute a separate, compliant data processing agreement or data sharing addendum prior to the transfer of any such personal data
findings.why: A separate data processing or sharing agreement is required before any other personal data is shared.

findings.quote: fixed period of three (3) years from the Effective Date
findings.why: A three-year term with a 30-day early termination right is within the accepted 1 to 3 year range.

findings.quote: for a period of five (5) years from the effective date of such expiration or termination
findings.why: Survival of five years is within the accepted 2 to 5 year range.

findings.quote: shall continue in full force and effect without limitation in time for so long as such information retains its legal status as a Trade Secret
findings.why: Indefinite protection is limited to Trade Secrets only.
findings.fallback_cited: Indefinite protection limited to Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief, specific performance, restraining orders
findings.why: Equitable relief is available to the Disclosing Party, so mutual, with no bond; the wording is strong but mutual.
findings.fallback_cited: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.

findings.quote: shall be cumulative and shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, any other rights
findings.why: Equitable remedies are expressly cumulative, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: in accordance with the substantive laws of England and Wales
findings.why: English law governs.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Neither party may assign without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited, subject only to mandatory law.

findings.quote: shall immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual, suspected or threatened unauthorised access
findings.why: Imposes an immediate duty to report actual, suspected or threatened misuse and to cooperate in remedying it, which no playbook rule covers.
